scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

| **Personal routine** | Routines create predictability, which can lower anxiety and improve time management. | You’re less likely to skip other important tasks because you’ve already “checked off” a key part of your morning. |

### A few ways to keep the momentum going

1. **Set a timer** – If you’re worried about spending too much time, a 10‑minute timer can keep you on track while still giving you that ritualistic feel.
2. **Pair it with another habit** – For example, after trimming, do a quick stretch or a short gratitude journal entry. The transition can reinforce the sense of preparedness.
3. **Reflect on the impact** – At the end of the week, jot down how you felt before and after your grooming routine. You might notice patterns that reinforce its value.
